episode_title: 7MS #745: Securing Your Family During and After a Disaster – Part 10

real_qa.q: What should you document in an emergency family information security plan when you manage all household finances and bill payments?
real_qa.r: Create a shared Google Doc with all critical information your family might need, including access to password vaults, insurance policy details, passport renewal dates, car tab expiration dates, and house maintenance schedules like HVAC filter changes and water softener maintenance. Point the document to passwords, insurance policies and their details, and use automation tools like N8N and SimpleFin to keep financial account information automatically updated in Notion so family members can access current balances and transactions even if you are no longer alive.
real_qa.requete: emergency family financial security documentation plan

real_qa.q: How can you discover unknown financial accounts a family member may have opened decades ago?
real_qa.r: Request statements from all financial institutions and be alert when receiving statements from accounts you do not recognize. One discovery came when the spouse received a statement from a Credit Union account the deceased had opened with his mother years ago and kept after her death, maintaining himself as primary owner without adding his spouse as a co-owner, which went unnoticed until reconciling accounts after his death.
real_qa.requete: discover unknown old bank accounts after death

real_qa.q: What multi-factor authentication backup plan should you have if your phone is lost or damaged in an emergency?
real_qa.r: Use passkeys when possible instead of phone-based multi-factor codes, and add a backup phone number to accounts so your spouse can receive multi-factor tokens. This ensures critical financial and bill-pay accounts remain accessible even if your primary phone with multi-factor codes is no longer available.

real_qa.q: What is SimpleFin and how can it help automate financial account monitoring for family emergency preparedness?
real_qa.r: SimpleFin is a read-only access tool you can connect to online banking accounts to pull down balances and transactions daily. You can set up a script that automatically categorizes and tags transactions with account numbers and pulls them into Notion, creating a centralized shared view of all checking, savings, 401k, and other accounts that updates itself automatically even if you are not alive.
real_qa.requete: SimpleFin automated financial account tracking Notion

real_qa.q: What employment-related investment accounts might you not know your spouse has set up?
real_qa.r: Some employers auto-enroll employees in investment accounts that deduct portions of paychecks without the employee's active memory of enrollment. One discovery came when an old coworker notified the spouse of a significant investment account the deceased pilot had been enrolled in by the airline he flew for, which HR confirmed was real and contained a substantial sum of money.

real_quote: If you need to know everything that is going on with literally all accounts including checking savings for us the kids the 401k all the things, go to Notion. It will be updating itself, even if I am not alive.
